item: A newsletter removal that fails partway says how many articles are removed and how many are left, and the salvage's epoch bump is strict (queue item 58)
summary: Queue item 58, two follow-ups from PR #1865 (the coordinator, 2026-11-09 03:51Z). BEFORE: (a) delete_imported_newsletters removes in chunks of 900, each committed with a strict corpus-epoch bump; a chunk that failed (one of its deletes, or its bump) escaped as whatever the failure was, so POST /api/newsletters/remove-imported answered a bare 500 while the earlier chunks were already removed and Keyword.mention_count/article_count and the per-source counters still counted them (the counter repair ran only after the last chunk), and the settings panel kept the count it had before. (b) repair._after_the_swap bumped the epoch non-strictly, so a failure was swallowed inside bump_corpus_epoch, which handed back the epoch the damaged file already had, and the repair report's corpus_epoch read as if bumped. NOW: (a) a failed chunk is rolled back whole, the counters are refreshed for the chunks already removed (only when one was), and NewsletterRemovalStopped (a RuntimeError, raised outside the handler so the failure is not chained to it) carries removed, total and counts_refreshed; the failure is logged scrubbed where it happened. The route answers 500 in those fixed words, through http_detail, e.g. 'The removal stopped after removing 4 of the 5 imported newsletter articles; the other 1 is still in your corpus. Run the removal again to remove it.', plus 'Until then, some keyword and source counts may read high.' when the refresh also failed, or 'The removal stopped before it removed any of the N ...' for a first-chunk failure. Counters that cannot be refreshed after a complete removal no longer turn it into a 500: the 200 carries counts_refreshed false and a note in fixed words, which the panel shows in a warning toast, as text: the panel itself hides once nothing is left to remove, which is exactly when the note comes. The panel refreshes the remaining count after a stopped removal too, so it shows the stopped removal's words beside what is left. (b) the bump is strict=True: a failure reads None and the log says 'the corpus epoch was not bumped (<type>); until the next epoch bump the keyword rollup may count mentions the repair could not keep and miss new mentions that reuse their ids' (the type only, as the repair logs; keyword_mentions.id has no AUTOINCREMENT, so an id at or below the rollup's watermark can be handed out again, and its incremental merge reads only ids above it). On the base a failed bump was already logged, by the bump itself; what read as if bumped was the repair record's post_steps.corpus_epoch. The per-day keyword counts need nothing more: Salvage._finish already marks them unbuilt in the copy (pinned in tests/test_day_counts.py). TESTS: tests/test_partial_removal_and_salvage_epoch_item58.py, 13, through the real removal, the real write gate and the real route (TestClient over a file-backed store; only the failures are planted, a planted needle never reaches the answer), the salvage bump also through the real session_scope; and tests/newsletter_remove_node_test.js, the panel's two functions extracted from the shipped engine and run in order (the note reaches the user although the panel hides, a stopped removal leaves the panel with its words and what is left, one POST each), driven from the Python file. On 787366d50, with the new names imported behind a guard (the base has none of them), 12 of 13 fail and the control (a working salvage bump reads the new epoch) passes; the node suite fails there and on the first build of this change (f92d471cf) on 'the note reaches the user'. MUTANTS: 16 on the first build, all killed; 18 on the folded head, all killed (the salvage bump non-strict, no rollback of a failed chunk, the refresh run when nothing was removed, the raise inside the handler, the chunk counted before it commits, the words' counts clause, singular and plural, the counts swapped, the success note and flag, the refresh helper claiming success, the route without its catch, the panel's count refresh only on success, the note put back in the panel, the note dropped, the note toasted as ok, the repair log without the id-reuse lag, a first-chunk failure worded as a removal). INDEPENDENT READ (Opus): NO-GO on one must-fix, folded: the note was appended to the panel, which the count refresh then hid (their node probe: the panel display none, the only toast 'ok'). Should-fixes, folded: the release line now says the repair record, not the log, and names the keyword-trend summary, not every keyword cache; the lag names the id reuse; prune is no longer listed among the bumps (R632: it does not always bump); this row's base count was stated without its method. Optional, stated below: opening the counter-deferral marker. NOT CHANGED: a removal that stops because the process ends (not a failure) leaves the counters stale until it runs again, as stated in its docstring; the counter deferral marker (R22) is not opened by a removal, so the counters keep reporting exact until refreshed; after a failed salvage bump the columnar rollup keeps counting what the repair lost until the next epoch bump (stated in the log, not retried); a raise after a chunk's commit but still inside its handler (the bump's own log line, the gate's release) would leave that committed chunk uncounted, so the words would overstate what is left, the safe direction, and running it again finds the truth; if the count read after a stopped removal fails, the panel hides with its words, as the panel always did when it could not read the count. Release-notes line: «Removing imported newsletters no longer ends in an internal error when it fails partway: it says how many were removed and how many are left, and running it again removes the rest. After the app repairs a damaged library file, its repair record now says when the keyword-trend summary was not told to rebuild, instead of reading as if it was.»
